Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent
with cervical whiplash injury. The mechanism of injury described is plausible for a collision of this type. Over the course of 26
visits, care included conservative managemnet with manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home stretching program
instruction. Cervical imaging and physical examination findings clearly confirm the soft tissue injury, with reduced range of
motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness documented at initial evaluation. No prior injury or treatment to the cervical spine is
known. The treatment course followed a typical progression, with visit frequency tapering as symptoms improved and range of
motion returned toward normal. Billing records reflect one charge per scheduled service, with no duplicate or repeated entries. At
discharge, the patient was improving, with residual mild stiffness and a plan for independent home exercise.
